judgments.title: NG YIN PIN v DEREK KWOK KEE YEUNG & ors
judgments.catchwords: 1 . This is a divorce proceeding commenced by Ng Yin Ping ("the Petitioner Wife") against Derek Kwok Kee Yeung ("the Respondent Husband"). In the Petition, the Petitioner Wife seeks, inter alia, various reliefs arising from the breakdown of the marriage. The Petitioner Wife has also named Olga, Marianne Rostaqui ep. Petithomme ("the Co-Respondent") as the Co-Respondent in respect of allegations concerning the Respondent Husband's alleged adultery with the Co-Respondent. 2. The Respondent Husband filed his Answer to the Petition and Cross-Petition dated 26 November 2025. In his Cross-Petition, the Respondent Husband named Kang Cheow Sean ("the Party Cited") in respect of allegations that the Party Cited was involved in an adulterous relationship with the Petitioner Wife. The Respondent Husband further seeks, inter alia, an order that the Party Cited pay damages to him for adultery. 3. The present judgment concerns the Party Cited's application in Enclosure 19 to be struck out and/or removed as a party to the Respondent Husband's Answer and Cross-Petition. The application is made pursuant to Order 18 rule 19 and Order 92 rule 4 of the Rules of Court 2012, read with rule 103 of the Divorce and Matrimonial Proceedings Rules 1980. 4. The issue for determination is whether, in the circumstances of the present case, the Party Cited ought to be struck out and/or removed as a party to the Respondent Husband's Answer and Cross-Petition on the grounds that the pleadings disclose no reasonable cause of action against him and/or that his inclusion is scandalous, frivolous, vexatious or an abuse of the process of the Court.

judgments.title: Pendakwa Raya v CHAN WEN JIE
judgments.catchwords: Child Act 2001 – Section 31(1)(a) – Ill-treatment of child – Guilty plea – Caregiver entrusted with custody of 3-year-old child – CCTV footage showing repeated abuse including caning, slapping, striking victim's head, forcing squat-thrusts, prolonged standing and consumption of excrement – Victim sustained 44 superficial injuries – Whether sentence should reflect cruelty and humiliation inflicted upon victim. Criminal Sentencing – Principles – Balance between public interest and offender's interest – Court required to consider seriousness of offence, aggravating and mitigating factors and sentencing trends – Sentence must be proportionate to offence actually convicted. Mitigation – Guilty plea – First offender – Remorse – Cooperation with authorities – Prompt medical assistance rendered to victim – Discount available for early plea though capable of reduction where offence involved significant cruelty. Aggravating Factors – Breach of trust – Accused paid to care for victim – Victim aged three years and unable to defend himself – Repeated abuse resulting in 44 injuries – Humiliating and degrading treatment – Forced consumption of excrement constituting exceptionally cruel conduct. Sentencing – Withdrawn charge – Murder charge under s 302 Penal Code subsequently withdrawn – Withdrawn charge cannot be treated as aggravating factor – Accused to be regarded as innocent of withdrawn charge. Sentencing – Relevant facts – Victim's death – Medical evidence showing death not subject matter of conviction – Death cannot be considered as aggravating factor where accused convicted only of child abuse under s 31(1)(a) Child Act 2001. Sentencing Trend – Section 31 Child Act 2001 – Cases involving death or grievous injuries generally attracting imprisonment of 10 years or more – Cases involving superficial injuries attracting sentences ranging from 15 months to 5 years – Present case justified higher sentence due to extreme humiliation and cruelty. Evidence – CCTV recording – Objective visual evidence of repeated abuse – Court entitled to place substantial weight on CCTV footage demonstrating nature, frequency and degree of mistreatment inflicted on child victim. Child Abuse – Humiliation as aggravating feature – Forcing victim to eat excrement from diaper found to be an extreme form of mistreatment and degradation – Serious aggravating factor warranting enhancement of custodial sentence beyond ordinary abuse cases involving superficial injuries. Sentence – 8 years and 6 months' imprisonment from date of arrest – Bond of good behaviour with one surety for three years – Community service of 36 hours within six months pursuant to s 31(2) Child Act 2001. Ratio Decidendi: In sentencing under s 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001, the court must impose a punishment proportionate to the offence of conviction and cannot take into account a withdrawn murder charge or the victim's death if they do not form part of the conviction. However, exceptional cruelty, humiliation, breach of trust and sustained abuse of a vulnerable child may justify a substantial custodial sentence notwithstanding the presence of mitigating factors and an early guilty plea. Keywords: Child abuse; ill-treatment of child; caregiver; breach of trust; guilty plea; sentencing principles; aggravating factors; mitigating factors; CCTV evidence; humiliation; forced consumption of excrement; proportionality; withdrawn charge; victim's death; Child Act 2001; community service.
judgments.judge: YA Dato' Abdul Fareed bin Abdul Gafoor

judgments.title: MOHD RAIZAN BIN MAKHOZAINI v Pendakwa Raya & ors
judgments.catchwords: Undang-undang jenayah — Rayuan jenayah — Akta Dadah Berbahaya 1952 — Penggunaan dadah bagi kegunaan sendiri — Seksyen 15(1)(a) — Seksyen 39C(1) — Hukuman — Rayuan terhadap hukuman — Hukuman penjara tujuh tahun dan tiga sebatan — Sama ada nyata berlebihan — Ketagihan dadah — Pemulihan — Prinsip perkadaran — Faktor mitigasi — Sabitan terdahulu — Sama ada hukuman maksimum wajar dikenakan — Hukuman sebatan — Perintah pengawasan di bawah seksyen 38B Akta Dadah Berbahaya 1952. Diputuskan, rayuan Perayu dibenarkan: Perayu telah disabitkan di bawah seksyen 15(1)(a) Akta Dadah Berbahaya 1952 dan dijatuhi hukuman di bawah seksyen 39C(1), iaitu penjara selama tujuh (7) tahun, tiga sebatan (3) dan pengawasan selama tiga (3) tahun di bawah seksyen 38B Akta Dadah Berbahaya 1952 yang bermula selepas tamat tempoh hukuman penjara. Dalam rayuan terhadap hukuman, Mahkamah Tinggi mendapati bahawa hukuman tersebut adalah nyata berlebihan. Mahkamah mengambil kira sifat kesalahan, keadaan ketagihan Perayu, tanggungan keluarga, pekerjaan, sabitan terdahulu dan prospek pemulihan. Mahkamah Tinggi memutuskan bahawa aspek pemulihan merupakan pertimbangan penting dalam kes penggunaan dadah bagi kegunaan sendiri dan hukuman maksimum tidak wajar dikenakan. Sehubungan itu, rayuan Perayu dibenarkan dan hukuman yang dijatuhkan oleh Hakim Mahkamah Sesyen yang bijaksana diketepikan dan digantikan dengan hukuman penjara selama enam (6) tahun, satu (1) sebatan dan pengawasan selama tiga (3) tahun di bawah seksyen 38B Akta Dadah Berbahaya 1952 setelah tamat tempoh hukuman penjara.

judgments.title: KHAIRUL AZWAN BIN CHE ISMAIL v Pendakwa Raya & ors
judgments.catchwords: Criminal Law – Criminal Appeal – Section 354 Penal Code – Outraging Modesty – Use of Criminal Force – Intention and Knowledge – Credibility and Reliability of Complainant – Material Discrepancies in Evidence – Corroboration – Section 157 Evidence Act 1950 – Reasonable Doubt – Defence Evidence – Failure to Cross-Examine – Unchallenged Evidence – Burden of Proof – Unsafe Conviction – Acquittal and Discharge. Held, appeal allowed: The appeal concerns the Appellant's conviction under Section 354 of the Penal Code for allegedly outraging the modesty of a driving test candidate. The Appellant contended that the complainant's testimony contained material inconsistencies concerning the nature and manner of the alleged physical contact, which were not corroborated by the evidence of subsequent statements made to other witnesses. The Appellant further maintained that the contact was merely an instinctive response to a driving emergency involving a manual vehicle rolling backwards on a slope. The Prosecution's failure to challenge this explanation in cross-examination further supported a reasonable doubt. Accordingly, the Appellant is acquitted and discharged.

judgments.catchwords: CIVIL PROCEDURE: Injunction – Interlocutory injunction – Plaintiff suing to rescind shareholders’ agreement and loan agreement for misrepresentation, fraud and deceit – Application to restrain defendant, a 40% shareholder, from receiving dividends from company pending trial or, alternatively, for dividends to be paid into plaintiff’s solicitors’ client account as stakeholder – Whether bona fide serious issue to be tried – Whether alternative prayer mandatory in nature requiring unusually strong and clear case – Whether damages adequate remedy – Dividends purely monetary and precisely quantifiable – Whether damages adequate where claim founded on misrepresentation and fraud – Whether bare assertion of risk of non-recovery sufficient absent evidence of impecuniosity or dissipation – Whether plaintiff could obtain what was in substance a freezing order without satisfying requirements of Mareva injunction – Balance of convenience – Whether injunction would preserve or alter status quo – Delay – Undertaking as to damages – Burden on applicant to show means to meet undertaking – Rules of Court 2012, O 29. COMPANY LAW: Shares – Dividends – Registered shareholder’s entitlement to participate in dividends as and when declared – Minority shareholder without control – Company declaring dividends not party to suit – Whether order restraining shareholder from receiving dividends declared by non-party company would intrude into its internal affairs without company being heard – Withholding of defendant’s dividends and management of company in issue in pending oppression proceedings and contemplated derivative action before another High Court – Whether court should make interlocutory order that may pre-empt matters pending before another court – Whether proper party to complain of any wrong was company rather than plaintiff as its majority shareholder. EQUITY: Clean hands – Allegations that plaintiff blew hot and cold, relied on false statutory declarations and failed to disclose related proceedings – Whether necessary to determine where application failed on other limbs – Alleged falsity of statutory declarations subject of ongoing police investigations – Whether resolvable on affidavit evidence.

judgments.title: Pendakwa Raya & ors v Julasiri Bin Akilmara
judgments.catchwords: Offence under section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 read together with section 34 of the Penal Code - Whether the trial judge should have informed at the close of the prosecution's case, that the defence was being called upon to answer a case of actual trafficking or presumed trafficking? - Overwhelming evidence proved the elements of custody, control, and knowledge - Actual possession of the impugned drugs was established - Section 180 (1) and (4) of the Criminal Procedure Code - Procedure after conclusion of case for prosecution - No statutory or legal requirement to state the presumption when calling for the defence - Formal verbal label for an evidentiary rule at the close of the prosecution's case is unnecessary - Statutory presumption of trafficking under section 37(da)(xvi) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 - Section 422 of the Criminal Procedure Code - Not vitiate the conviction - No miscarriage of justice - Failure either to make or to record such a finding does not ipso facto - The law does not require a mini-judgment or detailed legal reasons at the close of the prosecution’s case
